explanation: Aluminium displaces iron from iron(III) oxide in this highly exothermic reaction, producing molten iron directly - used to join railway tracks and repair cracked machine parts.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A mixed grey powder of reddish-brown iron(III) oxide and silvery aluminium.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A glowing pool of molten iron, alongside solid white aluminium oxide.

thermal.visual_cue: Blinding white sparks and light, with molten iron visibly glowing orange-white as it forms.

beaker_view.observation: Once ignited, the mixture flares into blinding white sparks and light, and molten iron can be seen pouring out, glowing orange-white with heat.
